generated_response: Veto power refers to the ability of a legislature to prevent or modify an action that has already been enacted by a higher authority. In other words, it is a power of resistance against what has been decided upon by another body. This can include things like blocking legislation, refusing to vote on a bill, or vetoing executive decisions. The concept of veto power is often seen as one of the checks and balances in a democratic republic, where multiple branches of government work together to ensure that no single person or institution can dominate decision-making.
